findings.title: B3 M12 stated residual model error (≤1e-6) is false by a factor of about 400 to 4e6
findings.detail: residual_model_error() and note §4.3 say B3 M12 has 'no self terms and a tiny dipole cross term: ≤ 1e-6'. It returns 8.9e-11 at 100 Hz and 8.3e-7 to 1.0e-6 at 5–80 MHz. The closed form puts every inter-wire mutual at fil_mutual(centre distance). That is exact only for the harmonic log part of the finite-length kernel. The non-log end terms (+d − d²/4l …, with transverse Laplacian μ0/2π(1/d − 1/√(l²+d²)) ≠ 0) average to M(p) + (s/4)∇²M, where s = E|u−v|² is r² for uniform current and 2r² for surface current. This is the same first-order ⟨d⟩ mechanism that §4.1 fixed for self terms, but the fix was not carried over to mutuals between different wires. A perfect L2 would therefore show B3 M12 err ≈ 4–8e-4 against u ≈ 1e-6. The level-1.0 'deterministic bound' would then report a spurious lower end of about 4–8e-4, attributed to L2. It does not flip the 2 % criterion. It does falsify the wire model error bound that this task was meant to fix, and the bound would be frozen at registration.
findings.evidence: Scratch check (python -c, nothing written to the repo). The exact uniform-current mutual of the B3 staples is the average of fil_mutual over the two disks, using the disk-line-picking pdf and quad with epsabs=0, epsrel=1e-12. It gives 2.699610 nH against the runner's 2.698561 nH: relative error 3.886e-4, stated bound 8.858e-11. Per pair: legs +220.6 fH each, tops +612.6 fH. In the thin-skin limit (axisymmetric surface current, 256×256 periodic trapezoid) it gives 2.700663 nH: relative error 7.79e-4, stated bound 1.0e-6. My hand estimate (r²/4)Σ±∇²M = 3.9e-4 agrees. The same mechanism adds about 2.1e-4 to B4, which stays within its stated 8.7e-4, and an estimated ~2e-4 to C1 through the image terms, which stays within 1.4e-3 thanks to the 1e-3 truncation allowance.
findings.suggested_check: Add (s/4)∇²M (or the exact disk/annulus average) to inter-wire and image mutuals, or add a stated term; then compare B3 M12 against a disk-averaged reference in closed_forms_independent_check.

findings.title: Refinement rule can declare convergence falsely when error is algebraic in the level index; the contract does not exclude this
findings.detail: remaining_discretization_error assumes the changes contract geometrically from level to level (observed ρ, floor 0.5, factor 1.25). That is valid only with a constant grid-refinement ratio in the asymptotic range, which is Roache's precondition. The L2 contract (§3) requires only that 'level k+1 must refine every discretization'. It sets no fixed ratio, so additive refinement such as nwinc = 2k+1 or n_seg = k is allowed. In that case the error goes as k^-p and the observed ratio tends to 1 while the estimator assumes ρ ≈ 0.5–0.6. The DoD convergence_estimator.py tests only exact geometric sequences, so it cannot catch this.
findings.evidence: Scratch run of R.remaining_discretization_error on L = 1 + 0.05 k^-p. For p=1 with 4 levels: estimate 5.21e-3, true 1.25e-2, so convergence is declared (<1e-2) while the true remaining error exceeds conv_tol. For p=1 with 5 levels: estimate 4.69e-3, true 1.00e-2, also declared. For p=2 with 5 levels: estimate 1.52e-3 against true 2.0e-3 (ratio 0.76).
findings.suggested_check: Require a fixed refinement ratio (e.g. h_{k+1}/h_k = 1/2 for every mesh parameter) in the §3 contract and have l2 report it in meta, or switch to an observed-order GCI that uses the actual mesh sizes.

findings.title: Interval recorded at level=1.0 includes a GCI-type estimate, not a bound
findings.detail: The width u_i adds the remaining discretization error, a Roache-style estimate with Fs=1.25, to stated residuals, several of which are labelled [I] in the note (the (a) stiffness argument and the (b) 8r/l end allowance). Roache presents GCI as an error band of roughly 95 % confidence, not a guarantee. Calling the interval a deterministic bound at level 1.0 therefore overstates it, as finding 1 already demonstrates for B3 M12.
findings.evidence: Runner l2_phase: run.metric(..., ci=(lo, hi), level=1.0); unc = disc_unc + model_err; note §4.3 marks the (a) and (b) arguments as [I].
findings.suggested_check: Describe the interval as an estimated error band, or keep level=1.0 only for terms that are proven bounds.

findings.title: solver_tol contract treats the iterative residual tolerance as Z accuracy and ignores conditioning
findings.detail: §3 defines meta['solver_tol'] as 'the iterative relative-residual tolerance, plus the accuracy of any matrix compression' and treats it as the relative accuracy of Z. The forward error of a GMRES solution can reach κ(A) times the relative residual. PEEC systems with graded filaments (R_i ∝ 1/A_i spread over orders of magnitude) can have κ ≫ 1. The l2_solver_tolerance check (B3 needs ≤ 4.1e-8, which I reproduced) can therefore pass while the error in L exceeds solver_err_budget.
findings.evidence: Note §3 'Solver accuracy'; solver_tol_required(B3) = 4.11e-08 in my scratch run; no conditioning term in solver_tol_required.
findings.suggested_check: Require a direct factorization at the LF bar and wire comparisons, or require solver_tol to include a κ estimate or an a-posteriori Z error estimate.

independent_checks_performed: Ran all six definition-of-done commands. mfos exp check E001, ruff, --analytic-only, b1_exact_limits.py, convergence_estimator.py and design_contract.py all pass.

Read the three DoD scripts. They test B1 only (single wire, no mutual), exact geometric sequences only, and the presence of keys and strings. None of them tests mutual-term model error or non-geometric convergence.

B3 M12 at DC. Computed the exact uniform-current mutual of the two staples (fil_mutual averaged over two disks via the disk-line-picking pdf, Gauss angle quadrature and quad with epsabs=0) and compared it with the runner's analytic M12 and residual_model_error(B3, f, 'M12'). Result: 3.89e-4 actual against 8.9e-11 stated.

B3 M12 in the thin-skin limit. Axisymmetric surface-current average (spectral trapezoid in two angles). Result: 7.79e-4 actual against about 1e-6 stated at 5–80 MHz. A hand derivation of (s/4)∇²M gives the same size.
Propagated the same M12 gap to B4 (2.1e-4 against a stated 8.7–9.3e-4, so the bound holds) and estimated it for C1's image terms (~2e-4 against a stated 1.4e-3, so the bound holds).

Adversarial inputs for remaining_discretization_error: algebraic sequences k^-1 and k^-2 over 3–5 levels. Convergence is falsely declared for k^-1 at 4 and 5 levels, with the estimate 0.42–0.47 of the true error.
Searched the note's §3 refinement contract for a refinement-ratio requirement. There is none; only 'refine every discretization' is required.
Reproduced solver_tol_required for B3 (4.11e-8, matching the note) and reviewed its derivation for a conditioning term. None is present.
caveats: Bash was restricted: no ls or heredoc, and nothing could be written to /tmp. All scratch checks were run as inline `uv run python -c` against the runner at this commit, and no repository files were modified.

No L2 solver run was possible. moduleforge.solvers.l2 is a later deliverable, so the L2-path checks (l2_converged, solver tolerance, one mesh per solve) were reviewed only by reading the code and testing the estimator on synthetic sequences.

The B3 M12 defect does not change the 2 % pass/fail criterion. It is rated blocker because the claim is that the wire model error bounds are correct, and the wrong bound would be frozen at registration as part of a level-1.0 'deterministic bound'.
I did not re-verify the tube-PEEC, Carson and dipole self-checks independently beyond confirming that they pass; they were not tuned on the B3 M12 quantity.
